checks.finding: REQ-003's advisory/required byte-identity requirement is impossible as written on the Full track, and AC-016/TEST-016 lock that impossibility into an acceptance criterion. (1) EXACT TEXT: REQ-003 (requirements.md:463-481) states that the same inputs under either enforcement state 'produce byte-identical output across this invocation's own track-exclusive output set (... the three Full-track artifacts `facet-manifest.yaml`/`project-context.resolved.json`/Resolver Evidence ...); within that set, only Resolver Evidence's own `state` field and its two enforcement-derived `context_binding` digest fields -- `full_context_revision` and `projection_sha256` ... -- differ'. The same sentence's own 2026-08-24 amendment parenthetical gives the reason those two digests must differ: 'each is a hash of canonical bytes that themselves encode `workflow.capability_enforcement` -- the canonical Project Context text and the canonical Context Projection text, WHICH COPIES `workflow` VERBATIM'. `generated/project-context.resolved.json` IS that canonical Context Projection (REQ-001 step (c); AC-003; AC-044's `dependency_pointers[]` = '/workflow' plus one '/components/<id>' per affected component), and `workflow.capability_enforcement` is by REQ-003's own derivation rule a member of `workflow`. Therefore the published projection file itself differs byte-for-byte between an otherwise-identical advisory/required pair -- while REQ-003 and AC-016 (requirements.md:897) and TEST-016 (acceptance-tests.md:65) all place it inside the byte-identical set and name only Resolver Evidence's three fields as exceptions. The same defect reaches the second Full-track artifact: REQ-004 fixes Resolver Evidence's `context_binding` as 'identical shape to Epic A4's own `contextBinding` definition' and AC-005/AC-051 confirm `facet-manifest.yaml` carries that same `context_binding` (registry_digest, dependency_pointers), so `facet-manifest.yaml`'s own `full_context_revision`/`projection_sha256` must differ by the identical argument, yet the exception is scoped textually to 'Resolver Evidence's own ... fields'. (2) DOWNSTREAM FAILURE MODE: the verifier building the AC-016/TEST-016 `enforcement-byte-identity` Full-track fixture pair cannot satisfy the criterion by any correct implementation -- the byte comparison fails on `project-context.resolved.json` and on `facet-manifest.yaml`'s two context_binding digests -- and cannot decide which of three mutually exclusive repairs the specification intends: (a) drop those two artifacts from the comparison, (b) widen the named exception set to those artifacts' `context_binding` digests and the projection's own `workflow` block, or (c) restrict AC-016 to the Lite track, whose output set publishes no projection. Each is a different reviewable decision with a different fixture and a different scope of guarantee. (3) SPEC-STAGE OWNERSHIP: the contradiction is entirely between two Phase 1 sentences in requirements.md (REQ-003's byte-identity claim and REQ-003's own parenthetical rationale) plus their two restatement sites AC-016 and TEST-016; no design, task, or quality-gate artifact is needed to see or to fix it, and both restatement sites are inside this gate's input set. (4) SEVERITY: Critical under the calibration's 'impossible acceptance criteria' class -- AC-016 is not merely ambiguous, it is unsatisfiable by construction on the Full track, exactly the 'internally impossible' defect the B(1) amendment (investigation.md 'Rulings' section, commit `b572fcd65292b1652e6c03f8a08b26e6d8507160`) was raised to remove; that amendment reached the three statement sites it enumerates but scoped its exception to Resolver Evidence alone, leaving the two sibling Full-track artifacts asserting the impossible.
